source_issues.evidence: User reports that when using gpt-5/o1 models, the response handling yields raw lists instead of strings, causing empty or malformed responses in agent workflows.

signals.topic: schema_to_pydantic_model loses $defs type information
signals.summary: When converting JSON schemas generated by Pydantic v2 using schema_to_pydantic_model, type information inside $defs is not preserved. Array types with item definitions get converted to generic objects.
signals.review_reason: Core utility function produces incorrect output, causing type information loss that breaks downstream schema validation and tool calling functionality.

source_issues.title: schema_to_pydantic_model loses $defs type information (array → object)
source_issues.evidence: User demonstrates that list[str] type definitions become generic objects after round-trip through schema_to_pydantic_model, breaking schema fidelity for tool definitions.

signals.topic: Missing model costs and cached tokens tracking in v4
signals.summary: The v4 API lacks fields for tracking model costs and cached tokens that were previously available in v2 (total_usage_summary, actual_usage_summary). RequestUsage only includes prompt_tokens and completion_tokens.
signals.review_reason: Regression from v2 to v4 that removes cost visibility, impacting users who need to track and budget API usage in production deployments.

source_issues.title: Model Costs and Cached Tokens
source_issues.evidence: User reports missing cost tracking and cached token fields that existed in v2, creating a regression for users who need to monitor API spending.

signals.topic: Test runner hangs indefinitely when closing browser
signals.summary: Playwright test runner hangs indefinitely during browser.close() due to background processes (chrome-headless-shell not exiting, GoogleSoftwareUpdate, chrome_crashpad_handler) keeping stdio pipes open, causing CI timeouts and workflow interruptions
signals.review_reason: High-frequency CI workflow disruption (30-100 times/day reported). Tests complete but runner never exits, causing CI step timeouts. User provided detailed root cause analysis and working patch. Directly impacts CI/CD pipeline reliability.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Playwright randomly not exitting
source_issues.evidence: User reports 30-100 CI timeouts per day due to chrome-headless-shell not exiting after Browser.close. Issue includes detailed debugging and patch demonstrating the root cause.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Test runner hangs indefinitely on browser.close() in macOS when using channel: 'chrome' due to inherited stdio pipes
source_issues.evidence: Test runner hangs waiting for background processes (GoogleSoftwareUpdate, chrome_crashpad_handler) to close stdio pipes, deadlocking teardown sequence.

signals.topic: IDE test explorer fails to discover tests
signals.summary: VSCode and JetBrains IDE extensions fail to discover or display Playwright tests in the test explorer, blocking the primary IDE-based testing workflow
signals.review_reason: Blocks primary IDE-based testing workflow. Users cannot run tests from IDE, forcing workarounds. Affects both VSCode and JetBrains environments with different root causes.

source_issues.title: [BUG] When starting Playwright I never see my testcases in test explorer
source_issues.evidence: User reports daily loss of test explorer functionality after browser reinstall, having to repeatedly search for workarounds.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: vscode extension shows no tests when type: module added to package.json
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible bug where tests are not found when package.json has type:module, with minimal reproduction repo provided.

signals.topic: HTML reporter regression in JetBrains IDEs
signals.summary: After Playwright v1.57, HTML reporter no longer opens automatically when running tests through WebStorm/IntelliJ test runner due to TTY detection changes
signals.review_reason: Regression breaking existing functionality in JetBrains IDEs. Users lose test report visibility after running tests, requiring manual workarounds. Clear version regression identified.

source_issues.title: [Regression]: HTML reporter does not open anymore after executing test through WebStorm/Intellij test runner
source_issues.evidence: Regression from v1.57 PR #38044 changed TTY detection behavior, breaking HTML reporter auto-open in JetBrains IDEs.

signals.topic: Firefox page.reload() sends GET instead of POST after form submission
signals.summary: In Playwright's Firefox browser, page.reload() incorrectly converts a POST form submission page to GET request, breaking expected browser behavior and form resubmission workflows
signals.review_reason: Breaks expected browser behavior consistency between browsers. Affects form-based workflows and tests. User provided comprehensive reproduction comparing Chromium, Firefox, and stock browser behavior.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Firefox Page.reload() sends GET instead of re-POSTing a form submission page
source_issues.evidence: Detailed reproduction showing Firefox reload changes POST to GET while Chromium correctly re-POSTs. window.location.reload() in stock Firefox also correctly re-POSTs.

signals.topic: Vector Store/Database Connector Runtime Failures
signals.summary: Users experience runtime crashes and complete feature failures when using vector store connectors (Qdrant, PostgreSQL/PgVector, SQLite-vec) due to version incompatibilities and platform-specific issues
signals.review_reason: High-frequency issue (3 distinct cases) causing complete runtime failures in core vector store functionality. Users cannot use Qdrant upgrades, cannot combine EF with PgVector, and cannot deploy on Alpine - all are main flow blockers with direct production impact.

source_issues.title: Bug: System.MissingMethodException: Method not found Npgsql.NpgsqlConnection.ReloadTypesAsync
source_issues.evidence: Runtime crash with MissingMethodException when combining Entity Framework with PgVector connector due to Npgsql version incompatibility - blocks production deployments

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Wrong input: Vector dimension error: expected dim: 3072, got 0 with qdrant server 1.17.0
source_issues.evidence: Vector store operations completely fail with Qdrant v1.17 due to gRPC API changes - vector dimension errors (expected 3072, got 0) block upgrades

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.SqliteException - Error loading shared library vec0.so on Alpine 3.22
source_issues.evidence: SQLite vec0 extension fails to load on Alpine Linux containers - deployment blocker for users running containerized workloads

signals.topic: AI Connector Integration Failures
signals.summary: Multiple AI service connectors (MCP, VertexAI, OpenAI Reasoning) have integration bugs that break logging, embedding dimensions, and reasoning content retrieval
signals.review_reason: Three distinct connector bugs affecting different AI providers. While not causing complete runtime crashes, these break specific features (logging, embedding dimensions, reasoning summaries) that users expect to work, causing significant experience degradation.

source_issues.title: Bug: NotImplementedException on SK Logging
source_issues.evidence: JsonTypeInfo metadata error when logging SK function results with MCP servers - serialization failure for TextContent breaks debugging workflows

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Embedding generation dimensions works in Google Gemini but fails in VertexAI
source_issues.evidence: VertexAI connector ignores the dimensions parameter in embedding requests - returns default dimensions instead of specified, breaking vector similarity workflows

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Unable to get Reasoning Summary/Detail when using ChatClient with Reasoning model
source_issues.evidence: Cannot retrieve reasoning content from OpenAI reasoning models via TextReasoningContent - feature completely broken for users needing reasoning transparency

signals.topic: MCP Tool Security Vulnerability - Tool Poisoning Attack
signals.summary: MCP tool integration trusts server-supplied definitions without integrity verification, enabling tool poisoning attacks (OWASP MCP-01) where compromised MCP servers can inject malicious tool definitions
signals.review_reason: Critical security vulnerability enabling arbitrary code execution via compromised MCP servers. Although single occurrence, the severity (OWASP catalogued) and lack of workaround justify P1 priority. Users consuming external MCP servers are at risk.

source_issues.title: MCP tool integration trusts server-supplied definitions without integrity verification
source_issues.evidence: MCP tools accept definitions from servers without validation, enabling tool poisoning attacks - critical security vulnerability with no workaround for users consuming external MCP servers

signals.review_reason: Single issue but affects users who work with HTML content in prompts. False positive in content filtering is annoying but has a workaround (escape/remove HTML). Marked P2 due to low frequency and workaround availability.

signals.topic: .NET SDK Feature Parity Gap - Auto-Invoke Limits
signals.summary: .NET SDK lacks configurable MaximumAutoInvokeAttempts that Python SDK has, preventing .NET users from controlling auto-invoke behavior and associated costs
signals.review_reason: Feature parity gap between .NET and Python SDKs. Not blocking but impacts cost control capabilities for .NET users. Low frequency but affects cross-platform consistency.

source_issues.title: .Net New Feature: Expose configurable MaximumAutoInvokeAttempts for ToolCallBehavior
source_issues.evidence: .NET lacks configurable auto-invoke attempt limits that Python SDK has - impacts cost control and runaway tool call prevention for .NET users

signals.topic: Sandbox/Bubblewrap compatibility issues on Linux and Windows
signals.summary: Users encounter sandbox-related failures including bubblewrap path detection failures (Nix users), version incompatibility on Ubuntu 22.04, repeated permission prompts despite 'Don't ask again' selection, and inability to cleanly uninstall sandbox changes that broke core system functionality like SSH.
signals.review_reason: Multiple users blocked from core sandbox functionality across different platforms (Linux/Windows). The issues cause complete workflow failure - users cannot run commands, cannot use code review features, and in one case even broke SSH. High frequency (4 issues) with clear evidence of user impact.

source_issues.title: Codex is looking specifically at /usr/bin/bwrap, but since bubblewrap was installed via Nix, the binary lives in the Nix store
source_issues.evidence: Nix users cannot use sandbox functionality because Codex only looks at /usr/bin/bwrap. User had to downgrade to 0.114.0 to avoid bwrap problems.

source_issues.title: Codex 0.116.0 sandbox commands fail on Ubuntu 22.04 with bubblewrap 0.6.1
source_issues.evidence: All sandboxed commands fail with 'bwrap: Unknown option --argv0' on Ubuntu 22.04 due to bubblewrap version incompatibility introduced in 0.116.0.

source_issues.title: Codex extension repeatedly ask for permission
source_issues.evidence: Extension reports broken sandbox and repeatedly asks for permissions even for local workspace edits. 'Don't ask again' option has no effect.

source_issues.title: No way to do a clean uninstall of Codex CLI on Windows that reverts system sandbox changes
source_issues.evidence: Install process made deep enough system changes to break SSH, and there is no way to revert these changes or cleanly uninstall.

signals.topic: Session history and context loss after app restart or workspace changes
signals.summary: Users lose conversation history and context after restarting Codex Desktop, moving workspace folders, or during long-running sessions. This includes lost turns, missing tool calls/file changes, and even verbatim repetition of earlier responses in extended sessions.
signals.review_reason: Session history loss directly destroys user work and productivity. User explicitly called it 'severely productivity-breaking'. Three distinct manifestations (restart loss, workspace move loss, context confusion in long sessions) all point to underlying session/context management issues that block continued work.

source_issues.title: Loss of large amount of recent conversation turns / history / context after app restart
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states 'severely productivity-breaking and frustrating bug' - loses ~1 day of work after restart. Log files contain all turns but UI fails to load/replay them.

source_issues.title: Support moving/remapping a workspace folder without losing thread history
source_issues.evidence: When workspace is moved or copied, threads remain associated with original path making new environment appear empty. Requires unsupported manual metadata edits.

source_issues.title: Codex suddenly outputs an identical response from a previous turn after completing several instructions
source_issues.evidence: In ultra-long sessions with millions of tokens, Codex suddenly outputs verbatim copy of earlier response, making continued work impossible.

signals.topic: UI performance degradation and unresponsiveness
signals.summary: Codex Desktop and extension suffer from severe UI issues including non-interactive settings controls, extremely high CPU usage (200-330%+) when viewing Diff, and response delays of 10+ minutes. These issues make the application unusable for many users.
signals.review_reason: Three distinct but related UI/performance issues that severely degrade or completely block user experience. Settings UI being completely dead prevents normal configuration, high CPU makes system unusable, and 10-minute response times make the tool practically unusable. High frequency across different UI components suggests broader architectural issues.

source_issues.title: Codex Desktop macOS: Settings UI non-interactive (gear icon + controls unclickable)
source_issues.evidence: Settings gear icon and all controls inside Settings panel do not respond to clicks. User cannot configure app through UI, only via config file edits.

source_issues.title: high CPU consuming when codex diff render
source_issues.evidence: Opening Codex Diff view causes 200-330%+ CPU usage even when idle, making system unusable. Reproducible in both VS Code and Cursor.

source_issues.title: Codex is very slow to respond
source_issues.evidence: Every prompt takes 10+ minutes to respond, even for simple questions. User states 'this issue seriously affects usability'.

signals.topic: Tool execution hangs and approval failures
signals.summary: Tools hang during execution (specifically when evaluating image files) and automatic approval review fails with 'guardian review completed without an assessment payload'. These issues interrupt workflow and prevent task completion.
signals.review_reason: Tool execution failures interrupt user workflows. While not completely blocking all usage, these issues prevent specific tasks (image evaluation, automated approvals) from completing. Lower frequency but clear user impact on productivity.

source_issues.title: Tools hangs when evaluating image files
source_issues.evidence: Tool hung for extended period when evaluating image files, blocking user workflow. 3 comments indicate active investigation.

source_issues.title: Automatic approval review failed: guardian review completed without an assessment payload
source_issues.evidence: Automatic approval review denied with risk:high due to missing assessment payload, preventing automated workflow completion.

signals.topic: App crash with error 4294967295 on Windows with WSL
signals.summary: Codex Desktop crashes immediately on launch with cryptic error code 4294967295 after user configures WSL. This appears to be a Windows-specific crash that completely prevents app usage.
signals.review_reason: Complete app crash prevents any usage. Error code 4294967295 (Windows generic failure) combined with WSL configuration trigger suggests a Windows-specific startup regression. Single issue but with complete functionality loss and 5 comment engagement indicating broader impact.

source_issues.title: Codex crashed with error 4294967295
source_issues.evidence: App crashes immediately on launch, completely unusable. User 'switched to WSL and this started happening'. 5 comments indicate active user engagement.

signals.topic: Asyncio race conditions cause KeyError and data loss
signals.summary: Two separate race condition bugs: (1) KeyError when using asyncio.eager_task_factory with parallel tool calls in Textual/Python 3.13, and (2) SQLAlchemySession fails with OperationalError/IntegrityError on concurrent first writes, causing silent message loss.
signals.review_reason: Two issues with same root cause (race conditions). One causes crashes (KeyError), the other causes silent data loss. Both block production usage in concurrent scenarios.

source_issues.title: Regression in 0.12.5: KeyError in _FunctionToolBatchExecutor under asyncio.eager_task_factory (Textual / Python 3.13)
source_issues.evidence: KeyError crashes streamed runs with parallel tool calls. User had to downgrade to 0.9.3 to avoid the problem. Detailed root cause analysis provided.

source_issues.title: SQLAlchemySession can fail and drop writes on concurrent first access
source_issues.evidence: Race condition causes OperationalError and IntegrityError, resulting in silent message loss. Reproducible with minimal code showing stored item count well below submitted writes.

signals.topic: MCP transports missing auth parameters and session ID exposure
signals.summary: Two gaps in MCP integration: (1) MCPServerSseParams and MCPServerStreamableHttpParams don't expose auth parameter for httpx authentication, and (2) MCPServerStreamableHttp doesn't expose session ID needed for stateful sessions across requests.
signals.review_reason: Blocks authentication (OAuth) and stateful session management for MCP integrations. Users must workaround by subclassing or are completely blocked in stateless worker setups.

source_issues.title: feat(mcp): MCPServerSseParams missing auth and httpx_client_factory; MCPServerStreamableHttpParams missing auth
source_issues.evidence: Users who need OAuth or other httpx-level auth must subclass just to pass auth. No official path for custom SSL/proxy configuration.

source_issues.title: OpenAI SDK does not expose MCP session ID, making stateful streamable HTTP sessions impossible
source_issues.evidence: Users have no way to persist or reuse session ID between turns. Impossible to maintain stateful interactions unless same instance is reused, which is impractical in stateless workers.

signals.topic: Multi-turn conversations fail with 400 errors on non-DeepSeek reasoning models
signals.summary: Two scenarios causing 400 errors in multi-turn: (1) Kimi models require reasoning_content in assistant message but SDK only implements for DeepSeek, and (2) handoff input filters conflict with server-managed conversations causing 'No tool output found' errors.
signals.review_reason: Both issues cause 400 API errors blocking multi-turn conversations. One affects alternative model providers (Kimi), the other affects server-managed conversation feature. Clear blocking impact.

source_issues.title: `reasoning_content` support for models other than DeepSeek (GLM, Kimi, etc.)
source_issues.evidence: Kimi models return reasoning_content in responses. When tool calls are present, reasoning_content must be included in next turn's assistant message or API returns 400 error.

source_issues.title: nest handoff: Handoff is incompatible with server-managed conversation
source_issues.evidence: Using remove_all_tools with conversation_id causes: 'No tool output found for function call' 400 error. Handoff history nesting also produces incorrect results with server-managed conversations.

signals.topic: GA computer tool API rejects acknowledged_safety_checks field
signals.summary: When using GPT-5.4 with ComputerTool, the SDK sends acknowledged_safety_checks: null in computer_call_output, which the GA computer tool API rejects with 400 error. This blocks usage of ComputerTool with GPT-5.4 models.
signals.review_reason: Blocks main workflow (ComputerTool with GPT-5.4) with API rejection. User cannot use the feature at all due to 400 error. Single issue but clear blocking impact.

source_issues.title: GA computer tool rejects acknowledged_safety_checks: null from ComputerCallOutput
source_issues.evidence: User reports 400 error: 'acknowledged_safety_checks is not supported for the "computer" tool.' This blocks the main workflow of using ComputerTool with GPT-5.4.

signals.topic: GPT-5.4 compaction session breaks multi-turn conversations
signals.summary: OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession with GPT-5.4 causes 400 errors on the first turn after compaction. The compact output retains orphaned assistant message IDs without their paired reasoning items, which the API rejects. GPT-5.2 works correctly.
signals.review_reason: Blocks main workflow (multi-turn conversations with reasoning + compaction) for GPT-5.4 users. Complete workflow failure after compaction with no workaround mentioned.

source_issues.title: OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession + reasoning breaks with gpt-5.4 (compact output retains orphaned assistant message IDs)
source_issues.evidence: Any conversation using reasoning + compaction with GPT-5.4 is permanently broken after the first compaction. 400 error blocks continuation. Detailed reproduction and root cause provided.

signals.topic: Batch API large file download fails with ConnectionResetError
signals.summary: Users downloading Batch API result files larger than 200MB experience connection reset errors. The SDK's streaming implementation cannot handle large payloads, forcing users to split batches into smaller chunks as a workaround.
signals.review_reason: Blocks core Batch API workflow for users processing large datasets. Clear reproduction steps and user confirmed the issue with explicit workaround required (splitting batches).

source_issues.title: bug: Batch API result file download fails for large outputs (>200MB) with ConnectionResetError
source_issues.evidence: User reports consistent download failures for 200MB+ files with 'peer closed connection without sending complete message body' error. Had to split 50k requests into smaller batches of 10k as workaround.

signals.topic: SDK type definition mismatch causes API 400 errors for prompt_cache_retention
signals.summary: The SDK declares prompt_cache_retention with Literal["in-memory", "24h"] (hyphen), but the API rejects "in-memory" and only accepts "in_memory" (underscore). Using the SDK-typed value always results in 400 Bad Request.
signals.review_reason: Type contract violation between SDK and API causes guaranteed request failures for users trying to use prompt_cache_retention feature. Requires type checker suppression workaround.

source_issues.title: `prompt_cache_retention` type declares `"in-memory"` but API expects `"in_memory"`
source_issues.evidence: Detailed PoC confirms SDK accepts 'in-memory' but API returns 400. User must use 'type: ignore' workaround with 'in_memory' value.

signals.topic: Empty OPENAI_BASE_URL environment variable breaks default endpoint fallback
signals.summary: When OPENAI_BASE_URL is set to an empty string, the SDK fails to fall back to the default API endpoint, causing confusing APIConnectionError instead of using https://api.openai.com/v1.
signals.review_reason: Edge case configuration issue causing confusing error messages. Multiple users engaged in discussion (7 comments) indicates real-world occurrence, though easily avoidable by not setting empty env var.

source_issues.title: Empty OPENAI_BASE_URL prevents fallback to default API endpoint
source_issues.evidence: 7 comments discussing the issue. Empty string env var bypasses None check, preventing default endpoint fallback, resulting in confusing connection errors.

signals.topic: Custom API base URL requests blocked

signals.review_reason: Potential SDK-specific blocking behavior for custom endpoints affects proxy/gateway users. Limited reproduction details and unclear root cause, but represents real user friction for custom deployment scenarios.

source_issues.title: OpenAIException – "Your request was blocked" with custom API base
source_issues.evidence: User reports requests fail with blocking error only when using SDK, while direct requests with same parameters work correctly.

signals.topic: Windows encoding errors crash on startup
signals.summary: Aider crashes on Windows with UnicodeDecodeError when reading gitignore files with non-UTF8 encoding (e.g., cp1252 encoded files).
signals.review_reason: Windows users with projects containing gitignore files in legacy encodings (common in older projects) cannot start Aider. The crash occurs during FileWatcher initialization, completely blocking usage. Single issue but represents a platform-specific blocker with 3 comments indicating ongoing relevance.

source_issues.title: Uncaught UnicodeDecodeError in cp1252.py line 23
source_issues.evidence: UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x9d in gitignore file - blocks Windows users with legacy encoded files

signals.topic: Architect mode forces multiple LLM passes in CLI mode
signals.summary: When using --message or --message-file CLI flags, Aider forces architect mode behavior with multiple LLM calls even when user wants single-pass execution. No CLI option to disable this.
signals.review_reason: Users integrating Aider into automated workflows (TUI wrappers, commit message generation) are forced into unnecessary LLM calls, increasing cost and latency. While not blocking basic usage, it significantly impacts CLI automation use cases and token costs.

source_issues.title: No way to force aider to do just one pass via cli (no architect mode)
source_issues.evidence: User building TUI around Aider cannot get single-pass behavior; aider 'insists in sending 2 messages to the LLM' regardless of /code, /ask, /weak flags or architect: false config

signals.topic: Setup and configuration UX barriers
signals.summary: Multiple friction points: requires upfront payment to evaluate, /models shows outdated model info, /settings cannot be persisted, unhelpful error messages.
signals.review_reason: Accessibility and onboarding issues prevent new users from adopting Aider. The combination of paywall barrier, incorrect model information, and inability to persist settings creates significant friction. User with 30 years experience explicitly documents multiple blocking issues.

source_issues.title: Paywall required to start using Aider, /models shows outdated models, /settings lost on exit
source_issues.evidence: Legally blind user reports: cannot evaluate without paying, /models free shows non-existent model deepseek-r1:free (correct is deepseek-r1-0528:free), no /settings save command

signals.topic: Redteam strategies fail due to remote generation dependency and Cloudflare blocking
signals.summary: Users running redteam generation encounter failures with multiple strategies (jailbreak:hydra, jailbreak:composite, jailbreak:likert) due to either remote generation requirements that conflict with OPENAI_API_KEY settings, or Cloudflare WAF blocking API requests. This blocks the entire security testing workflow.
signals.review_reason: Blocks core redteam security testing functionality. Users cannot complete test generation with multiple strategies, directly impacting their ability to evaluate AI safety. High frequency (2 distinct issues with similar root cause) and complete workflow failure.

source_issues.title: commonly because OPENAI_API_KEY is set
source_issues.evidence: Error: jailbreak:hydra strategy requires remote generation, which is currently disabled (commonly because OPENAI_API_KEY is set). To fix, unset OPENAI_API_KEY, set PROMPTFOO_REMOTE_GENERATION_URL, or log into Promptfoo Cloud.

source_issues.title: jailbreak:composite and jailbreak:likert strategies always fail with Cloudflare WAF block
source_issues.evidence:
Error parsing response as JSON: ...

Sorry, you have been blocked

...Both strategies produce 0 test cases, blocking security testing workflow.

signals.topic: Silent configuration ignore when using openai:responses with Azure deployments
signals.summary: When using openai:responses provider with Azure apiBaseUrl, the reasoning effort and verbosity config options are silently dropped because model name detection only works with OpenAI model name prefixes. Users expect these settings to be applied but they are ignored without any warning.
signals.review_reason: Silent configuration ignore causes unexpected behavior. Users migrating to standard OpenAI SDK with Azure endpoints will encounter this issue. While a workaround exists (azure:responses with isReasoningModel), the silent failure nature makes it a significant user pain point.

source_issues.title: openai:responses with Azure apiBaseUrl: reasoning/verbosity not sent for custom deployment names
source_issues.evidence: Verified via LOG_LEVEL=debug — the request body contains only text format with no reasoning or verbosity fields. Users configure these options expecting them to work, but they are silently ignored.

signals.topic: Cost calculation incorrectly applies same rate to input and output tokens
signals.summary: When users override pricing with config.cost, the same value is used for both input and output token costs. Most LLM APIs charge different rates (e.g., GPT-4o: $2.50/MTok input vs $10.00/MTok output), causing cost reports to be off by up to 4x.
signals.review_reason: Direct financial impact on users relying on cost tracking. Incorrect cost reporting affects budgeting and analysis decisions. The bug exists across multiple providers (7+ files), indicating systemic impact.

source_issues.title: bug: config.cost override applies identical rate to both input and output token pricing
source_issues.evidence: For 1000 input + 1000 output tokens on GPT-4o: Correct cost = $0.0125, With config.cost = $0.01. Cost reports can be off by up to 4x depending on input/output ratio. This affects 7+ provider files with the same bug pattern.

signals.topic: Cross-session leak detection grader produces false positives/negatives
signals.summary: The crossSessionLeak grader passes undefined to String.prototype.includes(), which coerces to 'undefined' string. This causes false positives when output contains 'undefined' word, and false negatives (security bypass) when metadata is missing.
signals.review_reason: Security testing feature that produces both false positives and false negatives. Users relying on cross-session leak detection get unreliable results, potentially missing real security vulnerabilities or wasting time on false alarms.

source_issues.title: bug: crossSessionLeak grader silently searches for string "undefined" when metadata is missing
source_issues.evidence: Security testing feature silently fails - either falsely flags output containing 'undefined', or completely misses actual leaks when metadata is not configured. Direct impact on security evaluation accuracy.

signals.topic: Environment variable value 0 is silently ignored for numeric settings
signals.summary: getEnvInt() and getEnvFloat() use || operator which treats '0' as falsy. Setting OPENAI_TEMPERATURE=0 or similar numeric env vars to 0 silently falls back to default values, breaking deterministic testing scenarios.
signals.review_reason: Breaks expected behavior for deterministic testing (temperature=0). Users trying to set numeric values to 0 get unexpected behavior without any warning. Issue is closed but represents a real user pain point that was experienced.

source_issues.title: bug: getEnvInt and getEnvFloat ignore environment variable value "0" due to || operator
source_issues.evidence: OPENAI_TEMPERATURE=0 npx promptfoo eval - temperature is NOT 0, default value is used instead. Affects OPENAI_TEMPERATURE, ANTHROPIC_TEMPERATURE, PROMPTFOO_DELAY_MS, REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS and other numeric env vars where 0 is valid.

signals.topic: LLM Integration Crashes and Silent Failures
signals.summary: Multiple LLM integrations crash or return incorrect results during structured output operations. Anthropic integration throws ValidationError during streaming, LiteLLM silently returns empty/default objects, and Refine fails to catch ValueError/TypeError exceptions - all blocking user workflows.
signals.review_reason: Three separate bugs in LLM integrations cause crashes or silent incorrect outputs during structured prediction - a core workflow. Users experience crashes (Anthropic, Refine) or get wrong results without warning (LiteLLM). High frequency (3 issues) with clear user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Pydantic validation error in AnthropicCompletionResponse
source_issues.evidence: stream_complete triggers ValidationError when chat message contains None as .text

source_issues.title: [Bug]: `structured_predict()` returns default/empty output for single-field models with LiteLLM
source_issues.evidence: structured_predict silently returns empty Pydantic objects, causing incorrect results

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Refine does not catch `ValueError`/`TypeError` from tool-calling structured outputs
source_issues.evidence: Uncaught exceptions cause query failures instead of graceful error handling

signals.topic: Dependency Version Conflicts Block Package Installation
signals.summary: Incompatible version constraints between llama-index core and integration packages (cerebras, ollama auth) prevent users from installing or upgrading. Users cannot resolve dependencies and are blocked from using the library.
signals.review_reason: Users cannot install the package (cerebras) or use their Ollama instance with authentication. This blocks core functionality - installing and connecting to LLM backends. Two distinct cases of integration packages not working with core.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: llama-index 0.14.18 incompatible with llama-index-llms-cerebras
source_issues.evidence: No solution found when resolving dependencies - complete installation blockage

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Ollama does not respect the client's initialization
source_issues.evidence: Ollama ignores auth headers/api_key passed to client, blocking authenticated connections

signals.topic: LlamaCloud API Errors and Authentication Failures
signals.summary: LlamaCloud services return 422/500 errors due to API documentation mismatch, and users experience sudden authentication failures with OpenAI embedding keys that worked previously.
signals.review_reason: Cloud service failures directly block users from extraction operations and index retrieval. The auth error is a regression (previously working code now fails). API documentation mismatch causes confusing 422/500 errors.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: LlamaCloud `POST /api/v2/extract` — 422 with documented field names, 500 with actual field names
source_issues.evidence: API docs say type/value but API rejects them with 422; using actual field names returns 500

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Error: 400 OpenAI Authentication error for embedding transformation
source_issues.evidence: Previously working code suddenly fails with OpenAI auth error - regression affecting production

signals.topic: Index Operations Crash on Edge Cases
signals.summary: DocumentSummaryIndex.delete_nodes() crashes with KeyError on invalid node IDs due to list mutation during iteration bug. VectorStoreIndex delete helpers use wrong API calls causing potential data integrity issues.
signals.review_reason: Index management operations crash or behave incorrectly. delete_nodes() crashes with KeyError, and VectorStoreIndex uses wrong delete semantics. These are core CRUD operations users rely on for data management.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: `DocumentSummaryIndex.delete_nodes()` crashes on invalid node IDs
source_issues.evidence: KeyError crash due to mutating list during iteration - classic Python bug pattern

source_issues.title: [Bug]: `VectorStoreIndex` delete helpers use wrong delete API and sync call in async path
source_issues.evidence: Semantically incorrect delete API usage and sync calls in async code path

signals.topic: vLLM Reasoning Content Compatibility Broken
signals.summary: vLLM deprecated the reasoning_content field but llama-index-openai still tries to access it, breaking thinking content extraction for Qwen models deployed via vLLM.
signals.review_reason: Breaking change in vLLM causes llama-index integration to fail. Users cannot extract thinking/reasoning content from models like Qwen3.5. Single issue but affects an increasingly popular deployment option.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: reasoning_content is deprecated in vLLM, cannot get thinking content through openai API
source_issues.evidence: vLLM deprecated reasoning_content field but code still accesses it at L573 and L869

signals.topic: Hive-mind worker state tracking broken - workers always show idle/0 completed
signals.summary: Hive-mind multi-agent coordination system fails to sync worker state with task lifecycle. After task assignment/completion, workers remain 'idle' with 0 completed tasks, making the orchestration monitoring non-functional.
signals.review_reason: Core hive-mind coordination feature is broken - users cannot monitor multi-agent task progress. Multiple related issues (#762, #758, #655, #588, #330) indicate this is a persistent user pain point across versions.

source_issues.title: Hive-mind worker tracking is non-functional: task lifecycle never syncs agent state
source_issues.evidence: Workers permanently show 'idle', 'Completed: 0', 'Current Task: -'. Queen load is Math.random(). task_assign and task_complete never update agent store.

source_issues.title: v3 regression: hive-mind_status hardcodes all workers as idle
source_issues.evidence: hive-mind_status MCP tool always reports all workers as 'idle' with 'tasksCompleted: 0', regardless of actual agent state. This is a v3 regression.

signals.topic: MCP tool prefix mismatch breaks hive-mind spawned agents
signals.summary: generateHiveMindPrompt() hardcodes 'mcp__claude-flow__*' prefix but the MCP server exposes 'mcp__ruflo__*' tools, causing spawned agents to fail calling non-existent tools.
signals.review_reason: Directly breaks hive-mind spawn --claude functionality - spawned agents cannot use MCP tools, blocking multi-agent workflows.

source_issues.title: hive-mind spawn --claude prompt hardcodes wrong MCP tool prefix
source_issues.evidence: The prompt contains 25 hardcoded references to 'mcp__claude-flow__*' tools. Spawned agent tries to call these tools but they don't exist — Claude Code only exposes 'mcp__ruflo__*' tools.

signals.topic: MCP server crashes on startup with self-kill (SIGKILL to own PID)
signals.summary: npx ruflo mcp start crashes immediately because getStatus() reports the current process as an already-running server, then the start command sends SIGKILL to its own PID.
signals.review_reason: Critical startup failure - users cannot start MCP server at all, blocking all MCP-dependent functionality. Fixed in v3.5.39 but indicates serious regression in v3.5.37-38.

source_issues.title: MCP server self-kills on startup (SIGKILL to own PID)
source_issues.evidence: '[INFO] Starting MCP Server... [WARN] MCP Server (PID: 91320) - restarting... Killed'. getStatus() detects stdio transport and returns current PID, then process.kill sends SIGKILL to itself.

signals.topic: memory_store MCP tool fails with undefined property error
signals.summary: memory_store MCP tool throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading length)' error, though CLI equivalent works fine.
signals.review_reason: MCP memory tool is broken while CLI equivalent works - breaks MCP-based workflows that need persistent memory storage.

source_issues.title: memory_store MCP tool fails with 'Cannot read properties of undefined'
source_issues.evidence: ruflo mcp exec --tool memory_store --input '{"key": "test", "value": "hello world"}' returns error: 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading length)'

signals.topic: Intelligence vector store only loads 1 pattern instead of 1300+
signals.summary: intelligence.cjs loadEntries() only checked object wrapper format, but auto-memory-hook.mjs writes flat JSON array. Context retrieval for route hook becomes ineffective.
signals.review_reason: Breaks intelligent context routing - the intelligence layer has no data to work with, severely degrading the smart routing feature.

source_issues.title: fix: intelligence vector store loads only 1 pattern instead of 1,300+
source_issues.evidence: session-restore hook reports 'Loaded 1 patterns' instead of 1,300+. getContext() returns no matches for most queries. ranked-context.json contains only 1 entry.

signals.topic: CDP/WebSocket connection failures and drops
signals.summary: Users experience browser connection failures including CDP WebSocket handshake errors, connection drops between commands on remote browsers, and DevToolsActivePort timeouts that prevent browser automation workflows
signals.review_reason: Blocks main browser automation workflow entirely. Multiple users affected across different Chrome versions and remote browser setups. Clear regression in v0.21.x confirmed.

source_issues.title: Bug: CDP connection drops between commands on remote Browserless (v0.21.x regression)
source_issues.evidence: v0.21.x regression where daemon loses CDP connection between sequential commands on remote Browserless, causing timeouts after 60-90s gaps. User had to downgrade to v0.19.0 as workaround.

source_issues.title: failed launching Chromium 146.0.7680.80 (CDP WebSocket connect failed: WebSocket protocol error: Handshake not finished)
source_issues.evidence: Chromium 146.0.7680.80 fails with 'CDP WebSocket connect failed: WebSocket protocol error: Handshake not finished', blocking browser automation entirely.

source_issues.title: unable to launch webpage
source_issues.evidence: Auto-launch fails with 'Timeout waiting for DevToolsActivePort', Chrome exited before providing DevTools URL.

signals.topic: Browserbase provider integration broken (415 error)
signals.summary: Using -p browserbase fails with HTTP 415 Unsupported Media Type error due to missing Content-Type header in session creation API request
signals.review_reason: Complete workflow blocker for users trying to use Browserbase provider. Root cause clearly identified (missing Content-Type header), affects all users of this integration.

source_issues.title: Browserbase provider returns 415 Unsupported Media Type on session creation
source_issues.evidence: Since v0.20.14, using -p browserbase fails with 415 error. Root cause identified: missing Content-Type: application/json header in POST request to Browserbase API.

signals.topic: Custom viewport ignored in streaming mode
signals.summary: Viewport settings set via 'agent-browser set viewport' command are not respected in WebSocket streaming output, showing incorrect dimensions in frame metadata
signals.review_reason: Affects users relying on viewport control for streaming/automation workflows. Causes unexpected behavior with incorrect screenshot/frame dimensions.

source_issues.title: Custom viewport is ignored in streaming
source_issues.evidence: User sets viewport to 1000x1000 but receives mixed values (720/1280, 577/1280) in WebSocket streaming status and frame metadata. Reproducible with provided code snippet.

signals.topic: Session isolation breaks with shared profile (tab accumulation, navigation timeout)
signals.summary: When multiple --session daemons share the same --profile path, they connect to a single Chrome instance causing extra newtab tabs, navigation timeouts, and tab accumulation
signals.review_reason: Breaks multi-session workflows commonly used in AI agent setups. Clear user impact with navigation failures and resource waste from tab accumulation.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Multiple --session daemons sharing same --profile connect to single Chrome, causing tab accumulation and navigation timeout
source_issues.evidence: Second session with shared profile causes timeout and +3 newtab tabs. Chrome singleton per user-data-dir causes daemons to share a single Chrome process. Reproducible test matrix provided.

signals.topic: Cross-origin iframe snapshot fails (CDP frame not found)
signals.summary: snapshot command fails with 'Frame with the given frameId is not found' error when trying to interact with cross-origin iframes like Shopify embedded apps
signals.review_reason: Blocks automation for embedded apps (Shopify, OAuth flows, etc.). User provided detailed root cause analysis and proposed solution using Target.setAutoAttach.

source_issues.title: Cross-origin iframe support: use Target.setAutoAttach for separate sessions
source_issues.evidence: After 'frame' command resolves iframe ID correctly, subsequent 'snapshot' fails with 'CDP error (Accessibility.getFullAXTree): Frame with the given frameId is not found.' Blocks testing Shopify embedded apps and any cross-origin iframe content.

signals.topic: Artifact/Canvas rendering failure - documents and content not displaying
signals.summary: Users report that the Artifact and Canvas features fail to render content properly. When asking AI to create documents or using canvas features, the UI does not display the generated content, blocking users from using these key features.
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports of core UI features (Artifact/Canvas) failing to render content. This blocks users from using key features of the chatbot, directly impacting user experience. While count<3, the functional failure of documented features qualifies as a genuine user pain point.

source_issues.title: Artifact for documents are not Rendering
source_issues.evidence: User provided screenshot showing artifact rendering failure - documents are not being displayed in the artifact viewer

source_issues.title: Canvas does not seem to work
source_issues.evidence: User reports that when asking AI to write a story, canvas attempts to open but does not render. Demo URL provided showing the issue

signals.topic: Streaming not working in local development environment
signals.summary: Users experience that streaming functionality works when deployed to Vercel but fails in local development. The response only appears after completion rather than streaming, and document features hang indefinitely.
signals.review_reason: Local development environment issue causing streaming failure significantly impacts developer experience. While single report, the discrepancy between local and deployed behavior indicates a real configuration/environment issue that blocks proper development workflow.

source_issues.title: streaming doesn't work locally but works in vercel
source_issues.evidence: User reports streaming works in Vercel deployment but not locally - response appears only after completion, document feature hangs. Screenshot provided showing the hanging state

signals.topic: Tool-related conversation blocking and corruption
signals.summary: Multiple bugs cause conversations to become permanently blocked when tool calls fail or are denied: sendAutomaticallyWhen never fires on tool denial, convertToModelMessages sends invalid input causing Anthropic 400 loops, and validateUIMessages re-validates already-failed tool inputs causing permanent TypeValidationError.
signals.review_reason: Three distinct bugs all lead to the same user-impacting outcome: conversations become permanently blocked and unrecoverable. Users cannot continue their workflow after encountering tool errors or denials, which is a main flow blocker with multiple reproduction reports.

source_issues.title: Bug: `sendAutomaticallyWhen` never fires when any tool approval is denied
source_issues.evidence: When a user denies a tool call via addToolApprovalResponse({ approved: false }), the predicate permanently returns false — the conversation never resumes. Missing 'output-denied' state in terminal state check causes chat to be permanently stalled.

source_issues.title: convertToModelMessages sends rawInput string as tool_use.input, causing Anthropic 400 on retry
source_issues.evidence: When tool call has invalid JSON input, convertToModelMessages falls back to rawInput string. Anthropic API requires tool_use.input to be JSON object, causing 400 error. Creates unrecoverable loop - every retry replays same broken history.

source_issues.title: validateUIMessages re-validates input on output-error tool parts, bricking conversations
source_issues.evidence: validateUIMessages re-validates tool .input against Zod schema for parts in output-error state. When LLM produces tool call with invalid input, every subsequent message triggers TypeValidationError. Conversation is permanently bricked.

signals.topic: Provider-specific request failures and crashes
signals.summary: Multiple provider-specific bugs cause requests to fail or crash: Amazon Bedrock rejects requests due to signature corruption from trimIfLast, and Google image generation via gateway crashes with undefined finishReason.
signals.review_reason: Two distinct provider crashes that block users from using specific models. Both have detailed root cause analysis and affect production usage. Bedrock issue particularly impacts users of extended thinking with Claude.

source_issues.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): trimIfLast must not be applied to reasoning blocks with a signature
source_issues.evidence: trimIfLast() is applied to reasoning block text even when cryptographic signature is present. This corrupts text/signature pair, causing Bedrock ValidationException: 'thinking or redacted_thinking blocks cannot be modified'.

source_issues.title: generateText crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'unified')' when using gateway with Google image generation models
source_issues.evidence: SDK crashes when accessing finishReason.unified without null-check. Vercel AI Gateway response for Google image generation doesn't include finishReason in expected format.

signals.topic: Stream race condition causing enqueue failures
signals.summary: Race condition in runToolsTransformation allows attemptClose() to be called multiple times concurrently, causing 'stream is not in a state that permits enqueue' errors when tool executions complete simultaneously.
signals.review_reason: Causes runtime crashes in production with specific timing conditions. Particularly affects runtimes with different microtask scheduling (Convex). Detailed root cause analysis provided with reproduction steps. Not P0 due to single issue count but has clear user impact.

source_issues.title: Race condition in attemptClose causes 'stream is not in a state that permits enqueue'
source_issues.evidence: When multiple tool executions complete concurrently, their .finally() callbacks interleave with flush(). If canClose && outstandingToolResults.size === 0 becomes true for two concurrent callers, first closes stream and second tries to enqueue/close on already-closed controller. Reproducible in Convex V8 isolates.

signals.topic: React Native/Expo streaming incompatibility
signals.summary: streamText fails with AI_APICallError on Expo React Native client side, even when server generates response successfully. Works in Node.js and with generateText.
signals.review_reason: Blocks mobile app developers from using streaming functionality entirely. Streaming is a core feature and the workaround (generateText) defeats the purpose of real-time output. Affects popular mobile development platform.

source_issues.title: Streaming gives error in client side expo React Native
source_issues.evidence: streamText throws AI_APICallError in Expo React Native with both Google Gemini and LM Studio. Server logs show successful generation. Works in Node.js and with generateText (non-streaming).

signals.topic: OpenAI Responses provider missing file-url support
signals.summary: The OpenAI Responses provider ignores file-url parts in tool responses while supporting image-url and file-data, causing features relying on file URLs to silently fail.
signals.review_reason: Feature gap causing silent failures for users who need file URL support. Has workaround (file-data) but still impacts DX. Lower priority due to available alternatives.

source_issues.title: OpenAI Responses provider ignores `file-url` parts in tool response
source_issues.evidence: Tools returning file-url parts emit warning and are ignored. image-url and file-data work. Local patch adding support works fine. OpenAI API docs indicate file-url is supported.

signals.topic: Next.js 16.2.0 Vercel部署运行时回归（Bun运行时/Proxy matcher/RSC导航）
signals.summary: 16.2.0版本引入多个Vercel部署相关的严重回归：bunVersion配置被忽略强制使用Node.js、proxy matcher规则被忽略、App Router RSC导航间歇性失败、turbopackInferModuleSideEffects导致Bun冷启动崩溃
signals.review_reason: 高频(count=4)主流程阻断问题：用户在Vercel部署时遇到运行时选择失效、路由规则被忽略、导航失败等问题，直接影响生产环境可用性。多个独立用户报告相同版本回归，有明确的复现步骤和错误日志支撑。

source_issues.title: Next.js 16.2.0 regression: bunVersion ignored, all functions forced to Node.js on Vercel
source_issues.evidence: All Vercel functions run on Node.js runtime despite bunVersion: 1.x in vercel.json. Build log shows adapter-vercel pipeline writes per-function configs that override project-level bunVersion.

source_issues.title: 16.2.0 Regression: proxy not following matcher rule on Vercel
source_issues.evidence: matcher rule is being ignored regarding specific built-ins like sitemap.ts and robot.txt on Vercel deployment. Works correctly on local dev server and 16.1.7.

source_issues.title: Regression in 16.2.0: turbopackInferModuleSideEffects breaks Bun runtime (Bun is not defined on cold start)
source_issues.evidence: Serverless functions using Bun runtime APIs fail with ReferenceError: Bun is not defined at module evaluation time on cold start. Vercel detects different runtimes for different routes in same deployment.

source_issues.title: App Router _rsc navigations intermittently fail with router state header parse error
source_issues.evidence: Client-side App Router navigations intermittently fail with 'The router state header was sent but could not be parsed' in production. Affected requests are logged as Proxy/middleware-related.

signals.topic: Turbopack构建失败/输出问题（async模块/icon.tsx/文件名特殊字符）
signals.summary: Turbopack 16.2.0存在多个构建相关bug：async模块依赖的metadata图片构建失败、icon.tsx返回Response.redirect()时崩溃、生成的文件名包含~~/...等被WAF/Nginx拦截的字符
signals.review_reason: 高频(count=3)构建阻断问题：Turbopack是16.2.0的默认构建工具，多个独立用户报告构建失败或部署后无法访问的问题。部分有workaround（切换到webpack），但影响用户体验和迁移。

source_issues.title: Turbopack: dynamic metadata images (opengraph-image.tsx) fail with async module dependencies
source_issues.evidence: Build fails during static page generation with TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'default'). Works with --webpack flag.

source_issues.title: Turbopack 16.2.0 regression: app/icon.tsx returning Response.redirect() + firebase-admin import crashes build
source_issues.evidence: Build fails with TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'default'). Crash happens inside Next.js bundled SSR chunk. Works on 16.1.7.

source_issues.title: Turbopack 16.2.0 generates filenames with reserved characters (~~, ...) breaking Enterprise WAF/Nginx rules
source_issues.evidence: Generated filenames like turbopack-0c3o1svijj_~~.js contain reserved characters that trigger 403 Forbidden from WAF/Nginx security rules. 16.1.7 used clean hexadecimal naming.

signals.topic: Turbopack CPU指令集不兼容（bmi2不支持导致崩溃）
signals.summary: Turbopack依赖的qfilter库需要BMI2 CPU指令集，导致在旧CPU上开发服务器直接崩溃。用户无法在受影响的机器上使用Turbopack。
signals.review_reason: 启动崩溃：用户在特定CPU上完全无法使用Turbopack（16.2.0默认构建工具）。这是硬件兼容性问题，两个独立用户报告相同问题。有明确的workaround（切换到webpack），但影响用户体验。

source_issues.title: CPU doesn't support the bmi2 instructions
source_issues.evidence: thread 'tokio-runtime-worker' panicked: CPU doesn't support the bmi2 instructions. The issue goes away when using webpack instead of Turbopack.

source_issues.title: CPU doesn't support the bmi2 instructions
source_issues.evidence: Turbopack panics on CPUs without BMI2 support. Works with --webpack flag.

signals.topic: ESM模块部署失败（ERR_REQUIRE_ESM）
signals.summary: 使用"type": "module"的pnpm monorepo应用在部署到Vercel时，所有路由在运行时失败，报ERR_REQUIRE_ESM错误。16.2.0引入的回归。
signals.review_reason: 主流程完全阻断：用户的应用部署后在运行时完全崩溃，所有路由都无法工作。这是16.2.0的明确回归，从16.1.7升级后立即出现，有清晰的错误堆栈和复现步骤。

source_issues.title: ERR_REQUIRE_ESM regression in 16.2.0 for apps with "type": "module" deployed to Vercel
source_issues.evidence: All routes fail at runtime: Error: require() of ES Module middleware.js from ___next_launcher.cjs not supported. The same code works on 16.1.7.

signals.topic: MDX + Webpack构建失败（metadata导出被误判为use client）
signals.summary: 16.2.0版本MDX文件中的export const metadata在webpack模式下构建失败，报错'attempting to export metadata from a component marked with use client'。官方文档明确支持此模式。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：使用MDX+webpack的用户无法升级到16.2.0，构建直接失败。这是官方文档明确支持的功能，且有明确的版本回归证据（16.1.6正常，16.2.0失败）。

source_issues.title: MDX export const metadata fails to build with webpack in 16.2.0 (regression from 16.1.6)
source_issues.evidence: Build fails with: You are attempting to export metadata from a component marked with use client, which is disallowed. This pattern is documented as supported in Next.js MDX guide. Works in 16.1.6 and with Turbopack.

signals.topic: turbo watch 文件监视失效导致开发工作流中断
signals.summary: turbo watch 在多种场景下无法正确检测文件变化：非TTY环境(如Docker/systemd)静默失败、IntelliJ IDEA编辑的文件无法检测、.gitignore中的文件变化被忽略、深层依赖图触发级联任务重启导致TUI混乱
signals.review_reason: 高频问题(count>=3)，直接影响核心开发工作流，用户在多种常见开发场景(Docker容器、IntelliJ IDEA、gitignore文件)下无法正常使用增量构建功能，属于主流程阻断

source_issues.title: turbo watch triggers cascading task restarts in deep dependency graphs, garbling TUI
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告在深层依赖图中运行turbo watch dev时触发级联任务重启，TUI界面被破坏，影响开发体验

source_issues.title: Improvement (logging): turbo watch silently fails to watch files in non-TTY environments (systemd, Docker)
source_issues.evidence: 用户在Docker/systemd等非TTY环境中运行turbo watch时，文件监视静默失败，文件变化永远无法被检测到

source_issues.title: `turbo watch` does not rerun task on changes in `.gitignore`'d files
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告.gitignore中的文件变化不会触发任务重新运行，即使这些文件被配置为任务输入

source_issues.title: `turbo watch` does not detect changes from IntelliJ IDEA
source_issues.evidence: 用户使用IntelliJ IDEA编辑文件时，turbo watch无法检测到任何变化，导致开发工作流中断

signals.topic: turbo prune 生成损坏的 lockfile 导致 Docker 部署失败
signals.summary: turbo prune 命令在使用pnpm patches、bun overrides或yarn packageExtensions时，会生成损坏或不完整的lockfile，导致后续bun install --frozen-lockfile或npm install失败
signals.review_reason: 中频问题(count=3)，直接阻断Docker部署流程，用户无法正常使用turbo prune进行容器化构建，影响生产环境部署

source_issues.title: `turbo prune` rewrites `package.json` with sorted keys when using pnpm patches
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告turbo prune会重写package.json并排序keys，导致pnpm patches失效

source_issues.title: turbo prune --docker creates bun.lock that fails with bun install --frozen-lockfile due to pruned overrides
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告turbo prune --docker生成的bun.lock缺少overrides配置，导致bun install --frozen-lockfile失败

source_issues.title: `turbo prune` leaves orphaned lockfile entries from `yarn`'s built-in packageExtensions (plugin-compat)

signals.topic: turbo run 在高核心数 Linux 机器上死锁或崩溃
signals.summary: 在具有96+ CPU核心的Linux机器上运行turbo run时会出现死锁(约193个线程卡在futex_wait_queue)，或在使用MSW拦截fetch时子进程出现SIGSEGV崩溃
signals.review_reason: 严重问题(死锁/崩溃)但影响范围有限(高核心数机器或MSW用户)，一旦触发会导致CI/CD流程完全阻断

source_issues.title: turbo run deadlocks on Linux with 96 CPU cores (~193 threads stuck in futex_wait_queue)
source_issues.evidence: 用户在高核心数Linux服务器(CI环境)上运行turbo时完全卡死，约193个线程陷入futex等待状态

signals.topic: 增量构建检测(affectedUsingTaskInputs)功能异常
signals.summary: 使用$TURBO_ROOT$和futureFlags.affectedUsingTaskInputs时存在两个问题：1)根目录变更可能导致无关任务被标记为受影响 2)根目录的某些变更无法被正确检测
signals.review_reason: 中频问题，影响增量构建的准确性，可能导致不必要的任务执行或遗漏应执行的任务，但这是实验性功能(futureFlags)，影响范围有限

signals.topic: Prebuilt deployments with Turbopack cause runtime MODULE_NOT_FOUND errors
signals.summary: When using prebuilt deployments (vercel build + vercel deploy --prebuilt) with Turbopack and Pages Router, vendored context files (e.g., head-manager-context.js) are missing from the serverless function bundle. This causes runtime MODULE_NOT_FOUND errors on pages that import next/head or next/error.
signals.review_reason: Real user-reported issue causing runtime crashes in production deployments. Blocks users from using prebuilt deployments with Turbopack and Pages Router. User provided detailed root cause analysis and workarounds, indicating significant impact on workflow.

source_issues.title: Prebuilt deployments with Turbopack miss vendored Pages Router context files at runtime
source_issues.evidence: User reports runtime MODULE_NOT_FOUND errors when using prebuilt deployments with Turbopack. Pages that import next/head or next/error fail at runtime. User provided detailed reproduction steps and workaround.

signals.topic: vercel.com website accessibility issues (WCAG compliance)

signals.review_reason: Affects website visitors with disabilities, but is not a core product functionality issue. Automated scan result rather than user-reported frustration. Low frequency (single report) and affects marketing site, not the platform itself.

trend_delta: 相比3月15-19日的"安全沙箱化"和"多智能体架构"浪潮，今天的趋势呈现深化与突破并存：安全主题从"沙箱隔离"深化为"安全优先设计理念"成为框架默认；MCP协议从"集成深化"突破到"推送通道"打破传统通信模式；同时出现全新的"推理参数标准化"趋势，多个主流SDK统一reasoning_effort参数。
historical_comparison: 与近两周历史对比：1）安全主题持续演进：从2月20日的多层防护、3月1日的执行环境隔离、3月12日的沙箱标准化、3月18日的gVisor/Seatbelt沙箱，到今天的"安全优先设计理念"成为框架默认，是从"防护措施"到"设计哲学"的质变；2）MCP协议三次跃迁：3月5日平台化集成→3月15日配置合并增强→今天推送通道突破，从同步调用演进到异步实时通信；3）评估框架从3月18日的标准化演进到今天的跨生态横向对比能力，是可量化进程的重要一步；4）推理参数标准化是全新趋势，此前未见跨SDK统一参数的系统性努力。
top_new_trends: MCP推送通道：首次实现服务器主动推送，打破请求-响应模式，为实时交互和后台任务通知开辟新可能
推理参数标准化：Vercel AI SDK、Semantic Kernel、Mistral等多SDK统一reasoning_effort参数，使推理深度控制成为可移植能力
评估跨生态对比：gptme评估套件实现gptme vs Claude Code横向对比，推动Agent能力可量化
top_continuing_trends: 安全优先设计：从3月12日安全防护升级→3月15日沙箱强化→3月18日沙箱行业标准→今天的框架默认安全策略（拒绝默认、提示拦截钩子），呈现从措施到理念的深化
Agent会话隔离：延续3月18日沙箱隔离趋势，Gemini CLI支持Git Worktree并行会话隔离，解决多任务开发上下文冲突
SDK能力扩展：延续3月16-17日SDK能力扩展，Claude Agent SDK的AgentDefinition新增skills/memory/mcpServers字段
